questions.question: When parking downhill on a hill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: What should you do first when parallel parking between two cars?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop next to the car in front of the space you want.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the car in front of the space you want.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and signaling, stop beside the car that is in front of your parking space. Then turn your wheels and back in to park.

questions.question: How should you help cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep driving at the same speed in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for cars entering the freeway. If you can, move to another lane to give them space. If you cannot move lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: You are stopped in an intersection waiting to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and keep your wheels turned left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. This way, if a car hits you from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and carefully drive through.
Turn left or right since the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. After stopping, you can go when the road is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Look for cars only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before you or after you go first.
Look in all directions before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in all directions before going.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must stop completely and check for traffic in all directions before going.

questions.question: If a car has high beams pointing at you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when an oncoming car has bright headlights. This prevents you from being blinded and helps you stay on your course until the car passes.

questions.question: What should you do when a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and keep going.
Stop right away.
Stop before the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the light turns red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: At a yellow light, slow down and stop before you enter the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always stop completely.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be prepared to stop. Look both ways to make sure no trains are coming. Stop if you see or hear a train, and wait until it passes before crossing.

questions.question: When should you slow down when using a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Before you get on the exit ramp.
After you get on the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower cars on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you get on the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp. Once you are on the exit ramp, then slow down.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, where should you drive?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
Left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and see an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed lines mean drivers next to the line can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill on a curbed street, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel to the left.
Turn the steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, remove your foot from the accelerator, do not brake, and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, brake firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Hold the brake pedal down.
Pump the brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop a car in an emergency. Your car will stop quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop ahead.
Buggy warning.
Limited parking.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a stop sign is ahead and you should prepare to stop.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with four-way stop signs at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an intersection with four-way stops, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If the rear of your car is skidding to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, remove your foot from the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front in line with the rear and straightens your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
You only need to know roughly where you are going.
Always take the fastest route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you drive to an unfamiliar area. Know where you are going. Check a map to find your destination before you leave.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side where traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road that faces the traffic coming toward you. This helps you see vehicles approaching.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels go off the edge of the road. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the steering wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and apply the brakes gently. Slow down, check for traffic, and find a safe spot to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly, as this can cause you to lose control or hit other traffic.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and watch for other traffic. Look both ways before entering the intersection.
